policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Naioth' is a transliterated place name; the qere/ketiv difference is orthographic (מניות vs מנוות) and an English proper name cannot distinguish the spellings. Base qere fallback retained.
ASV 'my father doeth nothing either great or small' renders the negative לֹא of the qere לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה; the ketiv לו עשה ('for him he does') has no negation and would not yield 'doeth nothing'.
ASV 'the king sat him down to eat food' renders the preposition only as 'to eat'; either אֶל or עַל before the meal is compatible with that English. Base qere fallback retained.
ASV 'gathered up the arrows' is plural, matching the qere הַחִצִּים; the ketiv החצי is singular and would read 'the arrow'.
